h: Through the looking glass and onto the green
p: Here's a fun one to drop into conversation between holes: Lewis Carroll, the man behind Alice in Wonderland, had strong links with Guildford. His family lived in the town, and he's buried in the Mount Cemetery just above the river. There's even a little Alice statue by the castle grounds, so if your group has young readers in it, a hunt for that makes a nice add-on to the day. Quite fitting really, given that crazy golf is about as close to Wonderland logic as sport gets.

Practical bits first. Allow roughly an hour for a round, a bit more if you're a big group or you plan to stop for food and drinks. Turn up a little before your slot so you're not rushing, and if you've got very young children with you, it's worth checking the session times, as evening slots at places like this can lean more grown-up.

For something bigger, Guildford Cathedral sits up on Stag Hill on the edge of town, a striking modern red-brick building with great views back over the area. Theatre lovers have the Yvonne Arnaud Theatre by the river, and G Live hosts gigs and comedy nights. The University of Surrey keeps the town lively with students, which is part of why you'll find plenty of casual places to eat.
Fancy some fresh air afterwards? Newlands Corner and St Martha's Hill are classic Surrey Hills viewpoints a short drive out, perfect for walking off the post-golf snacks.
